name: Backgrounds Supply
tagline: 1,273 handcrafted and AI-made backgrounds in 29 packs, $49 once
description: Backgrounds Supply is a paid asset store that sells one large library of abstract backgrounds, gradients, textures and wallpapers, grouped into 29 named collections such as Gradient BGs (165), Smudge (112), Perplex (104) and Zephyr (83). One $49 payment unlocks lifetime access to every collection plus later additions, including a 36-file Animated Backgrounds pack. It is aimed at product, brand and motion designers who need a hero or slide backdrop immediately and do not want to generate one. A small free sample set sits at /freebies.
pricing_detail: $49 one-time payment for Unlimited Access, described as lifetime with future collections included. No refunds (digital goods). Free sample set at https://www.backgrounds.supply/freebies.
agent_guidance: Reach for this only when a human has already bought it and can hand you the image files — everything past the freebies page is behind a one-time paywall, so you cannot fetch assets at build time. When you do have the files, treat them as static hero/section backdrops (Figma, Framer, Photoshop, Canva, Webflow and After Effects are all confirmed to accept them) rather than as CSS you can generate; for a programmatic gradient you want a CSS or shader library instead. The site never states file formats or resolutions, so verify dimensions before you commit one to a full-bleed hero.
why_it_matters: Handcrafted background packs are the fastest way to make a generic Tailwind landing page look art-directed, and this is one of the larger curated libraries at a single flat price. The undisclosed file formats and the two conflicting counts on the page (1,273/29 in the header, 1,167/24 in the FAQ) keep it out of the top tier.

name: MotionSites
tagline: Paid copy-paste prompt packs for Lovable, Bolt, Cursor and Claude
description: MotionSites sells a library of ready-written website prompts that you paste into an AI site builder — Lovable, Bolt, Cursor or Claude — to get a finished hero, section or full landing page, with a heavy bias toward 3D and animated visuals. Prompts are filed under categories including Apps, Sections, Hero, Landing Page, SaaS, Agency, Portfolio, 3D Website, Travel, Ecommerce, Wellness, AI, Carousel, Fintech, Technology, Fashion and Healthcare. Part of the library is free to copy; the rest unlocks with an annual or one-time licence. It targets non-designers and solo founders who want a good-looking page without writing the prompt themselves.
pricing_detail: Free tier for prompts marked Copy. Go Unlimited $149/year or $239 one-time (all website prompts, no animated backgrounds or sections). Power $239/year or $349 one-time (adds animated backgrounds, page sections, future prompt drops). App prompts sold separately at $89/year or $129 one-time. Prices come from third-party directory listings — motionsites.ai/pricing returned 404 to a direct fetch.
agent_guidance: You are the tool this product is prompting, so there is almost nothing here for you to consume directly — the paid prompts are gated and the site is a Lovable-built SPA whose subroutes do not render to a fetch. If a user pastes one of these prompts at you, expect a maximalist 3D/animated spec (Three.js, WebGL, heavy scroll effects) and push back on bundle size, reduced-motion support and mobile performance before you build it. For a repeatable house style, a checked-in design.md plus a real component registry beats buying prompt text.
why_it_matters: It is a clear signal of where the market is going — prompts themselves are now a paid design asset — but the actual value is thin next to the price, and a well-written design brief you own outperforms a licensed prompt.

targets Lovable, Bolt, Cursor and Claude
3D and animated hero specialism
free tier of copyable prompts
up to $349 one-time for the Power tier

tier_reason: A js-only-shell SPA whose pricing route 404s, selling gated prompt text up to $349 that the record itself says a self-written brief outperforms.

name: Kaminari
tagline: Minimal Next.js 15 + Tailwind 4 + shadcn-ui starter, MIT
description: Kaminari is a deliberately bare Next.js 15 starter by lucky-chap (Huncho) that arrives with Tailwind CSS 4, shadcn-ui, TypeScript, ESLint, Prettier and `@`-prefixed absolute imports already wired up. It ships no marketing pages, no auth and no database — it is the empty-but-configured floor you build on, deployable to Vercel in one click. Use it when you want the shadcn toolchain without inheriting somebody else's product decisions. 358 stars, MIT, last pushed February 2026; the author lists Jest as "coming soon" and a version 4 as planned.
agent_guidance: Reach for this when the user wants a clean Next.js 15 + Tailwind 4 + shadcn project and you would otherwise spend three tool calls running create-next-app, `shadcn init` and fixing the Tailwind 4 config by hand — the one `create-next-app -e` command replaces all of it. It pairs naturally with any shadcn registry (shadcnblocks, Kibo UI, Magic UI) because the components.json and CSS-variable theme are already in place. Do not reach for it when the brief needs auth, billing or a database: it has none, so a SaaS boilerplate like next-forge or the official nextjs/saas-starter saves more work. Verify the Tailwind 4 config still matches current upstream before you scaffold — the repo is one maintainer's side project.
why_it_matters: Tailwind 4 broke a lot of older shadcn starters, and this one is small enough to read end to end in a minute while still being current — a rare combination for a scaffold you are going to inherit.

name: Homely Real Estate Template
tagline: $29 Next.js 15 + shadcn real estate site with listings and detail pages
description: Homely is a paid Next.js real estate website template from WrapPixel, built on Next.js App Router, React, Tailwind and shadcn/ui with TypeScript. The live demo ships a marketing home page (hero with a featured listing, four property-category cards, a six-property showcase grid, a featured-property spotlight, testimonials, a three-post blog strip, a CTA band, an FAQ accordion, a newsletter form and a footer) plus /properties, /blogs, /contactus, /documentation, /signin and /signup routes. It is for agencies and solo developers who need a property site delivered this week rather than a design system to build on. Listed at $29 with light/dark mode and reusable components.

name: Deck.gallery
tagline: 180 curated presentation decks, brand guidelines and reports
description: Deck.gallery is a curated gallery of beautifully designed presentation decks — 180 entries at last count — filed by type: Report, Guideline, Sales, Portfolio, Pitch, Marketing, Strategy, Talks and Other. It collects the real thing rather than mockups: Formula 1, Pleo, Zapier, Discord and Nike brand guidelines; Linear, Perplexity Ads and Yuga Labs pitch decks; Palantir Q4 2023, Strava Year in Sport and Mailchimp reports; portfolios from Studio Freight and other independents. Each deck gets its own page on the site, with a weekly newsletter and a small paid marketplace of deck templates alongside. It is a reference library for anyone who has to design a slide deck, a brand book or an annual report and wants to see how good ones are actually built.
pricing_detail: Browsing is free. A small marketplace sells deck and workbook templates — e.g. "Brand Strategy Workbook eBook Template $25".
agent_guidance: Reach for this when the brief is a deck, a brand book or an annual report rather than a screen — it is one of the few indexes of real, shipped presentation design, and the type filter (Pitch, Guideline, Report, Sales, Portfolio) maps cleanly onto a brief. The index page exposes a schema.org ItemList, so you can enumerate the 180 entries and their type from the HTML, but the decks themselves are images and PDFs: you can cite and link them, you cannot read the typography or grid out of them, so ask the user to look. Pair it with a type-specimen or colour source when you are actually producing slides — this gives you references and direction, never assets.
why_it_matters: Presentation design is badly under-indexed compared to web UI, and having Nike, Discord and Linear's real decks in one filterable place is a genuinely scarce reference for brand and narrative work.
